answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity cost real money: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it misbehaved. A raven of fake accounts would need one deposit per alias, so a Sybil flood becomes ruinously expensive while honest agents earn the deposit back through good work. Like an oasis guarded by a cedar, the registry stays open to newcomers yet costly to flood — the bond, not a password, is the gate.
